Subject: Private deployment pricing question – platform fee amortization vs ops retainer

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We are finalizing the internal procurement packet and a couple of questions came up from finance and procurement: is the platform fee you outline something we can amortize over our contract term for capex treatment, or is it strictly an operational retainer that must be expensed each period? If it can be amortized, how do you typically document the justification (invoice/ SOW language)?

Second, we need clarity on the difference between the ops retainer and the on-call SLA add-on — procurement sees overlap and wants a clear table showing which activities are covered under each line item (eg: escalation routing, runbook updates, monthly ops reviews, emergency on-call).

CCing audit@medisys.com for their visibility.

Best,

Medisys Health

Subject: Re: Private deployment pricing question – platform fee amortization vs ops retainer

Oliver —

Thanks for the clear ask. Short answer up front: the platform fee is typically structured to be capitalizable when customers purchase a perpetual license with an associated on-prem install and the fee represents a one-time entitlement for the software and deployment artifacts. The ops retainer is an ongoing service charge (monthly/annual) and is treated as OpEx.

Key points and what we can provide for your packet:
- Platform fee: one-time entitlement for the private control plane + deployment artifacts (installer, image, config templates). We can add specific SOW language that says "one-time entitlement amortized over useful life" to help your accounting.
- Ops retainer: covers runbook maintenance, scheduled DR tests, minor configuration changes, and low-severity triage within defined response windows. Billed monthly or annually — OpEx.
- On-call SLA add-on: purchased as a separate tier. Covers 24/7 severity-one responses, guaranteed escalation to engineering, and on-call incident management. This is explicitly not included in the base ops retainer.

I attached a brief term-sheet and an example amortization spreadsheet that shows how finance teams typically model the platform fee over a 3–5 year period. Also attaching the SLA tier CSV for the packet.

If helpful, Marissa can provide a pricing delta table (discount scenarios) and David can weigh in on the exact contract language we typically accept for amortization.

Would you like a one-page "procurement-friendly" summary we can hand to your finance team? I can turn that around by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Oliver,

Following up with the pricing perspective. We typically offer three packaging patterns for private deployments:

1) Perpetual license + one-time platform fee + optional ops retainer
   - Platform fee: list price $350k (example) — can be amortized by customer as capex; we provide invoice and SOW language to support capitalization.
   - Ops retainer: $8k/month — covers standard operational runbook maintenance and monthly reviews.

2) Subscription-style (multi-year committed)
   - Platform is spread into the committed price; allowed to be treated as OpEx in many customers' books depending on procurement policies.

3) Hybrid (staggered amortization)
   - Split platform fee into an "entitlement" portion (capitalizable) and an "implementation" portion (expensed) — we can design the split to match your internal policies.

Discounts and concessions: for deals in your band we can consider a staggered discount if you commit to a 36-month ops retainer; typical concession is 7–12% off platform fee and up to 3 months free on the retainer for annual prepay.

I'll let David add the legal/compliance caveats on exact wording for the SOW.

—Marissa

Oliver —

Couple of contract notes to be aware of if you plan to amortize:
- We can add explicit SOW language that the platform fee relates to a perpetual license and installation artifacts; however, we do not provide accounting advice — you should consult your finance team and auditors.
- If the platform fee is refunded or credits are applied later (eg, early termination concessions), amortization schedules may need to be adjusted — we'll include a clause describing credit handling.
- For dedicated upgrades or major re-installs after go-live, those are typically treated as separate billable items unless included in a negotiated implementation bundle.

I'll mark the specific SOW snippet and share as a short addendum for your procurement packet.

David Kim
Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
